findings.claim: The native-manifest open-task check has no cancelled/skipped exemption and has never been executed, so if tasks.json records skipped tasks 7/8 as done:false the archive gate deadlocks at the final step, after signed end-task has already completed canonical task 10.
findings.evidence: The guard exempts 'cancelled' in the canonical check (`!["complete", "cancelled"].includes(task.status)`) but the native check is `nativeTasks.tasks.filter((task) => !task.done)` with no status exemption. The change's own task list contains skipped tasks: tasks.md shows `- [ ] 7 … (SKIPPED)` and `- [ ] 8 … (SKIPPED)`, and the acceptance criteria generated from tasks.json omit tasks 6/7/8 entirely — consistent with tasks.json carrying them as non-done skipped/cancelled entries. The only guard receipt (archive-guard-pre-gate.md) exited at the earlier canonical check ('open tasks: 10'), so the native-manifest branch has never run; a mismatch would surface only after the point-of-no-return end-task transition.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the native filter with canonical semantics (`!task.done && !["cancelled", "skipped"].includes(task.status)`) and dry-run the guard's native-manifest check now, before signed end-task, to prove the final gate is satisfiable.

findings.claim: The fixture parity/hash check throws before the report object and try/finally exist, so a core/Flutter fixture drift failure produces no machine receipt even though task-9-packed-acceptance.json is the authoritative status record.
findings.evidence: The hunk places `readFile(coreFixturePath)`/`readFile(flutterFixturePath)`, `if (!coreFixture.equals(flutterFixture)) throw new Error("core and Flutter time-travel fixtures drifted")`, and the SHA-256 computation immediately after the corePackage lookup and before `mkdtemp`, the `report` object literal, and the `try {` block — so a drift failure bypasses report generation entirely while every other failure mode is recorded via the pending→pass status fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the fixture parity check inside the try block with a `fixture.parity: "pending"` initial status (mirroring `fixture.packed`), so drift is recorded as a failed status in the emitted report.

findings.claim: The new guard resolves the repo root via `import.meta.dirname`, which requires Node ≥ 20.11, while the sibling verifier imports `dirname` from node:path (the fileURLToPath compatibility pattern), leaving an unenforced runtime-version assumption inconsistent with the existing scripts.
findings.evidence: verify-kbd-archive-guard.mjs line 15: `const root = resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..");` — `import.meta.dirname` does not exist before Node 20.11. The pre-existing scripts/verify-devtools-time-travel.mjs imports `{ dirname, join, resolve }` from "node:path", indicating the established root-resolution pattern predates that API; no engines check or README note covers the discrepancy.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the root with `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))` to match the sibling script, or assert the Node version at startup.
